name: Seamec Ltd
title: Seamec Ltd - 526807 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Seamec Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41% YoY to INR 297 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124 crore (about 42% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 297 crore against INR 211 crore a year ago, up 41%, and standalone revenue was INR 283 crore against INR 201 crore. Consolidated PAT rose to INR 81 crore from INR 76 crore, while standalone PAT was flat at about INR 81 crore versus INR 80 crore. Management attributed the quarter to higher vessel deployment, healthy utilisation and cost discipline, with Paladin's dry-dock and the Middle East conflict weighing on the onshore segment. The call focused on the Seamec ANANT acquisition (USD 70 million, expected by end-August), the 40-42% margin band and the 15-20% growth CAGR target.

segments.name: Offshore (IMR/EPC vessels)
segments.commentary: Margins materially better than onshore, attributed to higher vessel deployment. Management said the 40-42% margin band is sustainable on an annualised basis.

segments.name: Onshore / other (Paladin)
segments.commentary: Margins pulled down because Paladin was non-operational in Q1 (dry-dock in Dubai, stuck by Middle East conflict); it incurred cost with no revenue. Paladin has returned to India and resumed contract, with revenue expected from Q2.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over the next 3-5 years and says it is committed to that number.
Margins: management guides 40-42% EBITDA margin, sustainable on an annualised basis; quarterly figures not guided.

Seamec ANANT: acquisition (USD 70 million, funded about 50:50 internal equity and loans) expected to complete by end-August 2026; deployment on ONGC contract about one month after acquisition for statutory formalities, with start expected within Q2 FY27 per Naveen Mohta and in Q3 per Sunil Gupta; expected 95-98% utilisation once working.
Gallant vessel sale: expected to complete in September 2026 after shareholder approval.
Seamec Princess/III: monsoon idle period (May-October); Princess being dry-docked in this period; contract talks for October at an advanced stage, not yet announced.
Seamec II charter ends end-August 2026; intended for EPC work rather than IMR; no rate uplift confirmed.

Management expects FY27 and FY28 growth from newer vessels and higher deployment; Samudra Samrat-type ONGC O&M contracts (Samudra Sevak, Samudra Prabha) continue, with no vessel-wise revenue disclosed.
capex_capacity: Seamec ANANT: USD 70 million purchase from HAL Offshore (binding agreement, related-party parent contract with ONGC); to be owned by Seamec post-completion.
Fleet: Seamec Princess dry-docking during monsoon idle period; Seamec Glorious (barge) off-hire in monsoon period; Seamec III and Princess off-hired.
Growth capex needed for incremental Middle East business since all current vessels are deployed (Sunil Gupta).
Non-core bulk carrier JV: one vessel liquidation agreement signed; OSV purchase in Dubai subsidiary abandoned.
MoU with DG Shipping for ~INR 1,000 crore of acquisitions over the next 2 years; management says it intends to grow the fleet but has no confirmed deal beyond ANANT.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for DSVs remains strong, with supply tight; expects strong demand for 3-5 years and says the Iran sanctions lifting could add more demand.
Management would not give a specific charter-rate outlook; rates depend on demand and supply.
Contract mix: about 35-40% of contracts are short term (EPC is short term, seasonal Oct-May); IMR contracts are mid to long term, some 3-5 years.
Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Abu Dhabi) cited as key growth area; Aramco qualification is helping inquiry flow, per management.
India: Andaman and Mahanadi discoveries cited as future opportunities in subsea, diving, inspection and maintenance.
Government's Samudra Manthan policy seen as supportive, but management said the benefit would take 3-5 years to show.

qa_highlights.question: Why are offshore margins better than onshore, and is Paladin contributing now?
qa_highlights.answer: Offshore margins improved on higher vessel deployment; onshore margin was dragged by Paladin's non-operational costs. Paladin has resumed operations and will contribute from Q1 onward per Naveen Mohta, with Sunil Gupta later saying the results will show in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Seamec ANANT: timeline, consideration and financing?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition expected by end-August 2026 under a binding HAL Offshore agreement for USD 70 million, financed roughly 50:50 between internal equity and loans. Vessel returns to the ONGC contract about a month after acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: How long will DSV charter rates stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific rate outlook given; management says rates depend on demand and supply and sees strong DSV demand for the next 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins move back to mid-40s?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management maintains 40-42% as the sustainable annualised band because of off-hire and dry-dock periods, and does not guide quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth targets and FY27/FY28 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with FY27 and FY28 growth from newer vessels and higher deployment; no quantified FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the royalty review (GT report) and the 4% revenue royalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an independent review by Grant Thornton was completed with a satisfactory report under consideration by independent directors; it will not be shared, and the 4% royalty to the parent continues.

risks_watch: Seamec ANANT: completion timing (end-August) and ONGC redeployment (Q2 vs Q3 guidance differs between management speakers); the USD 70 million acquisition is partly debt-funded.
Seamec II and Princess October contracts not yet announced; monsoon idle period leaves three vessels off-hire.
Middle East geopolitical exposure: Strait of Hormuz and Iran sanctions affected Paladin in Q1.
Related-party exposure: 4% royalty to parent continues; GT review report not being shared.
Contract mix: 35-40% of fleet on short-term contracts, so utilisation can swing with EPC seasonality.
Pearl bulk carrier in Dubai subsidiary under arbitration; bulk carrier JV liquidation in progress.
Unclear whether Samudra Manthan benefits will show within 2 years; management says 3-5 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and the 15-20% growth target, but noticeably vague on specifics: charter rates, contract names and timing are deferred to future exchange filings. Management was defensive on the royalty review and on the Seamec II rate question.
key_quotes: For Seamec, the Middle East remains a key growth market.
Management is committed for that number, and we are planning to do every bit in our scope to see that we achieve that growth.
So once it is finalized, we will be filing with the exchange so that everybody is aware about the contracts.
No. We -- I do not think we have ever conveyed that kind of impression that Seamec II will get hired on a higher rate.
But annualized basis, 40% to 42% margins are sustainable.

adds.what: Seamec ANANT vessel acquired from HAL Offshore for USD 70m (ONGC contract deployment after ~1 month statutory formalities)
MoU with DG Shipping for ~INR 1,000 crore of acquisitions over next 2 years (no confirmed deal beyond ANANT)

growth.why: Management reiterated 15-20% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years and ANANT (USD 70m) is expected to be deployed in Q2-Q3 FY27, but all current vessels are deployed, Seamec II charter ends Aug 2026, Princess/III are off-hired in monsoon, and no utilisation % or FY27 guidance was given.
